newsitem.title: TURKEY: Aid groups say work in N. Iraq facing obstacles.
newsitem.headline: Aid groups say work in N. Iraq facing obstacles.

text.p: Some aid agencies working in northern Iraq said on Tuesday that Turkey was blocking them from crossing into Iraq and this could hurt the distribution of food and medicine there under a U.N. oil-for-food deal with Baghdad.
Workers at some non-governmental organisations (NGOs) have not received permission from Turkish authorities to enter Iraq from Turkey since August, the agencies said.

Brian Smith, Iraqi field director for the British-based Save the Children Fund charity said from London that without the NGOs there was no "managerial capability" to implement the U.N. resolution under which Iraq will be able to sell $2 billion of oil over six months for food and medicine. Part of the aid will be directed to the Kurds in the country's north.

A Turkish Foreign Ministry spokesman has said restrictions were being imposed because of concerns about the activities of some aid groups. Turkey has in the past said the presence of aid groups benefited Turkish Kurd rebels based in northern Iraq.

Six French aid organisations said at a meeting in Paris last week that they were facing problems entering Iraq from Turkey, while Save the Children has also said its workers have not been allowed to cross.
